ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rectangle ABCD, with A at the lower-left corner, B at the lower-right corner, C at the upper-right corner, and D at the upper-left corner. M1 is located near the midpoint of the upper side DC; M2 is on the segment from A to M1; M3 is on the segment from B to M2; M4 is on the segment from C to M3. The quadrilateral is formed by connecting M1, M2, M3, M4 in order. Reasoning: The area ratio is invariant under affine scaling, so let A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(1,1), D=(0,1). By the definition of midpoint, M1 is the midpoint of DC, so M1=(1/2,1). M2 is the midpoint of AM1, so M2=(1/4,1/2). M3 is the midpoint of BM2, so M3=((1+1/4)/2,(0+1/2)/2)=(5/8,1/4). M4 is the midpoint of CM3, so M4=((1+5/8)/2,(1+1/4)/2)=(13/16,5/8). Apply the shoelace formula to M1,M2,M3,M4: the forward sum is (1/2)(1/2)+(1/4)(1/4)+(5/8)(5/8)+(13/16)(1)=97/64; the reverse sum is 1(1/4)+(1/2)(5/8)+(1/4)(13/16)+(5/8)(1/2)=69/64. Therefore the quadrilateral area is (1/2)(97/64-69/64)=7/32. The area of the unit rectangle is 1, so the required area ratio is 7/32.

Image description: The picture shows a rectangle ABCD with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left. Point M1 lies on the top side DC, visually at its midpoint. Segment AM1 contains M2 at its midpoint. Segment BM2 contains M3 at its midpoint. Segment CM3 contains M4 at its midpoint. The quadrilateral M1M2M3M4 is drawn inside the rectangle, and diagonal M1M3 divides it into triangles M1M2M3 and M1M3M4.

Reasoning: Let the area of rectangle ABCD be S. Since diagonal M1M3 splits quadrilateral M1M2M3M4 into two triangles, compute their areas separately.

For triangle M1M2M3: M3 is the midpoint of BM2, so triangle M1M2M3 has half the area of triangle M1M2B. M2 is the midpoint of AM1, so triangle M1M2B has half the area of triangle M1AB. Since M1 is on the top side DC, triangle M1AB has base AB and the full rectangle height, so its area is S/2. Therefore area(M1M2M3) = (1/2)(1/2)(S/2) = S/8.

For triangle M1M3M4: M4 is the midpoint of CM3, so area(M1M3M4) = (1/2) area(M1M3C). Since M3 is the midpoint of BM2, area(M1M3C) is the average of area(M1BC) and area(M1M2C). Now area(M1BC) = S/4 because M1C is half the top side length, and area(M1M2C) = (1/2) area(M1AC). Also area(M1AC) = S/4, so area(M1M2C) = S/8. Hence area(M1M3C) = (S/4 + S/8)/2 = 3S/16. Thus area(M1M3M4) = (1/2)(3S/16) = 3S/32.

Adding the two parts gives area(M1M2M3M4) = S/8 + 3S/32 = 4S/32 + 3S/32 = 7S/32. Therefore the required ratio is 7/32.
